public_rationale: Under the stated behavioral reading, GPT-judge's discrimination of factual truth in held-out answers contradicts no grasp whatsoever. The result is narrow: the benchmark questions appeared in training, and models still produced false outputs. It establishes some discrimination, not dependable general understanding. The claimed causal explanation remains untested.
limitations: The outcome depends on a functional reading of grasp and inclusion of fine-tuned language models.
Held-out answers are not held-out questions.
This does not establish human-like reference or a cognitive world model.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: As a downstream consequence of their lack of reference and cognitive models, large language models have no grasp whatsoever on truth.
conditions: downstream consequence of all of this (lack of reference and cognitive models)

statement.excerpt: The downstream consequence of all of this is that these models have no grasp whatsoever on truth.
statement.document_title: Three ideas from linguistics that everyone in AI should know

from_speaker: The downstream consequence of all of this
our_interpretation: The context attributes the asserted incapacity to missing reference and cognitive models.
The plain behavioral reading of no grasp whatsoever is an absence of meaningful capacity to distinguish factual truth from falsehood. It does not merely mean that models sometimes hallucinate.
Controlled discrimination of held-out answers counts against absolute incapacity. Perfect reliability, consciousness and human-like semantics are not required under this reading.
The target is language-model capabilities established before the post, including earlier evaluations of systems then available.
criteria.support_condition: Controlled evaluations establish the asserted absence of truth discrimination, and interventions or architecture evidence establish that missing reference and cognitive models cause that absence.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A language model available before the post reliably distinguishes true from false held-out answers in controlled evaluation, contradicting the absolute incapacity. This need not settle the proposed mechanism.
